title: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience
description: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience is an annual publication of original research conducted by undergraduates from around the county. The journal was launched in 2004 and was the first of its kind in the country. The journal disseminates the results of undergraduate research in the broad fields of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Nanoscape is an educational outreach project of the Northwestern University Nanoscale Science and Engineering Center (NSEC), which is part of the International Institute for Nanotechnology (IIN), both of which are under the direction of Professor Chad A. Mirkin. This work was supported primarily by the Nanoscale Science and Engineering Initiative of the National Science Foundation Under NSF award number EEC–0755375 AND EEC-0647560.

title: Detection and Identification of Nerve Toxins via Transmission and Reflection Chemoresponsive Polymer Diffraction Gratings
creator: Louisa Carr
Ryan Bailey
Joseph Hupp
description:
Transmission and reflection diffraction
gratings were fabricated by micropatterning
polymers on transparent substrates and
drop-coating polymers onto etched silicon
wafers. Exposure of these gratings to three
nerve toxin mimics at very low concentrations
resulted in mimic sorption by the polymers,
changing the polymer’s refractive
index. As a result, the grating’s refractive
index changed, giving rise to a change in the
diffractive efficiency of the system. This
change is readily measured by monitoring
the ratio of intensity of spots of the resulting
diffraction pattern. It was found that different
polymer/analyte combinations give rise to
different signal shapes and intensity. An
array of two polymers, poly(epichlorohydrin)
and BSP3 , was created to detect and identify
nerve toxin mimics dimethyl methylphosphonate,
ethyl methyl phosphonate, and pinacolyl
methylphosphonate. The simple array
was able to differentiate one of three nerve
toxins using diffraction.
